records.title: BEP: continue citation provenance and source re-audit
records.body:
## Research added

This continues the source-level citation audit on the integrated map without changing the independent v1 branch or merging any map.

- Reopened Urmès et al. (2022) at the publisher and re-audited its four abstract passages and 16 map links. The abstract supports a bounded dynamic kinetic-identification/model-fit precedent; it does not establish periodic performance gain, a matched optimized-steady comparison, or PdAg transfer. The full article and SI were not accessible.
- Audited the proposal's central question, steady-yield/equilibrium rationale, gas and surface equations, forcing-timescale heuristic, isothermal assumption, B-spline and gradient-search plans, validation plan, and hidden-state claims. These passages document proposal intent and assumptions, not validated scientific results.
- Reopened Zhu et al. (2021) through the Eindhoven University of Technology author-institution record. It describes a Pt/Al2O3 model-catalyst platform and CO oxidation, reports fast temperature pulses, increased reaction rates and lower power input, and attributes the rate response to simulation-based desorption/repopulation dynamics. This is a thermal-forcing analogy only. The accessible abstract does not give the proposal's “40-fold” number; the full article returned HTTP 403, so the magnitude is unresolved, not disproven. [TU/e article record](https://research.tue.nl/en/publications/novel-microreactor-and-generic-model-catalyst-platform-for-the-st/) · [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cej.2021.131559)

The proposal's steady-state-yield argument conflates a stationary flow-reactor state with thermodynamic equilibrium; its desorption/pulse/residence-time inequality remains an un-derived hypothesis. The proposed equations still need declared concentration, velocity, density, catalyst-rate and surface-site bases. A best feasible steady policy, matched cycle objective/constraints, and the relationship between selectivity and ethylene productivity remain open.

## Current audit coverage

- 143 nodes, 65 source records, 340 current claim-source links, and 96 historical citation attachments.
- 131 passage records and 89 short quotation records; 113 current links have passage IDs, 8 have derivation IDs, and 227 have neither.
- 13 source records were reopened; 52 source records remain unopened in source text.

- 115 links have an AI evidence recheck; 108 are partially supported and 4 remain unsupported/disputed at their inspected scopes.

The proposal now has 31 of 78 links with passages, leaving 47 unreviewed. The analysis does not assume periodic inlet forcing improves BEP performance and does not implement a simulator, fitting, or waveform optimization.

## Validation and limits

Focused PyYAML parsing covered all 340 claim-source records in bounded fragments, the new passage/claim/correction/batch records, IDs and reciprocal links, quote substrings, counts, and not_verified statuses. The proposal source hash and selected text were rechecked after commit; Urmès and Zhu source passages received separate post-commit re-audits.

records.title: Draft: opt-in non-PSSA coverage dynamics for reacting BEP reactor
records.body:
## Why this draft exists
The reacting vertical slice already solves transient **gas** equations but uses Urmès 2019 steady LHHW/PSSA **surface** rates. It does not yet solve time-dependent catalyst coverage balances. This draft adds an **opt-in and explicitly uncalibrated** elementary-step surface model, leaving the current reacting PSSA baseline unchanged.

## Implementation
- `3_Model/transient_surface_kinetics.py`: experimental Horiuti–Polanyi-family seven-step mechanism with 5 evolving adsorbate coverages, site balance, carbon/hydrogen inventory accounting and **no default kinetic constants**.
- `3_Model/vertical_slice_reacting_reactor.py`: opt-in `surface_params` for a 1D uniform-pellet path. Site-state feedback is real: gas production depends on the current coverages, not instant equilibrium. BDF uses numerical Jacobian in this mode until analytic/sparse Jacobian exists. Existing PSSA route unchanged by default.
- `3_Model/probes/test_transient_surface_kinetics.py`: 5 isolated unit checks; verified locally with NumPy (5/5 PASS). These are algebra/isolated model checks, **not** end-to-end reactor simulations.
- `research/notes/NON_PSSA_SURFACE_BRIDGE_2026-10-14.md`: source review, limitations, execution gates.

## Science gate — BLOCKING before any non-PSSA scientific result
1. Validate exact elementary network and source parameters from the *full* Urmès et al. (2022) paper (DOI 10.1002/cctc.202101826) and its supporting information; the 2019 **composite** LHHW parameters cannot simply be split into uniquely inferred elementary constants.
2. Obtain the actual `Methanol-Catalysis/pbr` source used by the existing reacting branch. The checked public `main` did not contain `pbr/`, so a clean GitHub-only execution was unavailable.
3. Execute full optional reactor in Codespaces: C/H and site invariants, admissible coverages, stiffness/Jacobian/convergence and prescribed pulse vs constant feed. Keep published PSSA rate baseline available and compare **only after** mechanism and parameters are reconciled.

**No reacting non-PSSA result, selectivity improvement, or source-derived transient time constants are claimed.** Please review physical assumptions and numerical implementation before merging.
